name: Default Mode Suppression
description: Task-positive suppression of default mode network (DMN) activity during externally-focused tasks. Brain deactivates self-referential processing (medial prefrontal, posterior cingulate, angular gyrus) when engaged in goal-directed behavior.
key_references: Raichle, M. E., MacLeod, A. M., Snyder, A. Z., et al. (2001). A default mode of brain function. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 98(2), 676-682.
Raichle, M. E. (2015). The brain's default mode network. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 38, 433-447.
empirical_evidence: Robust fMRI finding: DMN activity anticorrelated with task-positive regions during externally-focused tasks. DMN engagement during mind-wandering and rest. Lesion studies weak. Causal mechanism unclear: task engagement suppresses DMN, or DMN suppression enables task focus? Functional role debated (self-referential processing vs. others).

parameters.task_specificity: stronger for certain task types (external vs. internal focus)
